```{r libs_data}
library(conflicted)
library(tidyverse)
library(car)
library(survey)
library(srvyr)

df <- read_csv('../../data/unweighted_dataset.csv') |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
```

```{r formulas}
base <- SLD012 ~ RIDAGEYR + RIDAGEYR + RIDRETH3 + DMDEDUC2 + INDFMPIR

f_base <- update(base, . ~ . + ALQ130 + DUQ220U)
f_mental <- update(base, . ~ . + ALQ130 + DUQ220U + DLQ140 + DLQ100)
f_physical <- update(f_base, . ~ . + PAQ670 + PAD680 + BMXBMI)
f_interaction <- update(f_base, . ~ . + DUQ220U:DUQ219 + DUQ220U * ALQ130) # the colon here doesn't add DUQ219 as a main factor
f_interaction_and_physical <- update(f_physical, . ~ . + DUQ220U:DUQ219 + DUQ220U * ALQ130)

f_list <- list(f_base,f_mental,f_physical,f_interaction,f_interaction_and_physical)
```

```{r survey_weights}
library(survey)

full <- read_csv("../../data/full_data.csv")
full <- full |> 
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

# Because of survey design things that I don't understand the residual degrees of
# freedom are determined by the starta and primary sampling units. This means we 
# have a max cap on parameters we can have in our model and because we have so many
# categorical varaibles we were hitting this very fast, so we can test models with 
# limited combinations or we can bin the categorical variables into smaller bins

# for example the following formula leaves us with 0 residual degrees of freedom which as you can imagine is bad
# svy_formula <- SLD012 ~ RIDAGEYR + RIDRETH3 + DMDEDUC2 + INDFMPIR + BMXBMI + DUQ220U * ALQ130 

# I think we should drop education which frees up enough to add in the physical activity variables
svy_formula <- SLD012 ~ RIDAGEYR + RIDRETH3 + INDFMPIR + BMXBMI + PAQ670 + DUQ220U * ALQ130 

analysis_vars <- all.vars(svy_formula)

full_flagged <- full |>
  mutate(
    in_age_range = RIDAGEYR >= 20 & RIDAGEYR <= 59,
    complete     = if_all(all_of(analysis_vars), ~ !is.na(.x)),
    in_analysis  = in_age_range & complete & WTMEC2YR > 0 # need valid weights
  )

# full design
full_design <- full_flagged |>
  as_survey_design(
    ids     = SDMVPSU,
    strata  = SDMVSTRA,
    weights = WTMEC2YR,
    nest    = TRUE
  )

# We can just filter the design like a dplyr argument thanks to srvyr
analytic_design <- full_design |>
  srvyr::filter(in_analysis)

svy_mod <- svyglm(svy_formula, analytic_design)
summary(svy_mod)

```

The simpler base fit of this model shows that Non-Hispanic Black individuals have
a significant negative relationship with sleep hours on workday. We likely want
to add in more interaction terms. We have two options, summary(model, df.resid=degf(analytic_design))
which I am unsure of the justification of or we can do a set of models
stratified by race which we can then just compare estimates between (no longer 
testing statistically). This also allows for more residual degrees of freedom if
we want to add more parameters.

```{r set_df}
summary(svy_mod, df.resid=degf(analytic_design))

# Doing this we can also do more complicated designs if we want like adding in 
# an interaction between race and poverty index. As there there is likely no biological
# difference in needed sleep but there may be an interaction with socioeconomic status
# which likely impacts sleep

# https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42698981/svyglm-in-package-survey-in-r-not-returning-std-errors
# the way the svyglm operates is likely conservative, but just setting it to the
# design degrees of freedom is also liekly not fully correct


```

Survey object hold the data in svy_object$variables if you want to review the data
associated with the survey design object. Everything above should run without issue
and you should be left with:
* a survey design object `analytic_design`
* the unfiltered data `full`
* and the initial model `svy_mod`
